brief.situation: You configure the ticket router at Lakeshore Utilities (fictional). A foundation model on Amazon Bedrock labels each email with one of five queues. In testing, the same ticket gets different labels on different runs, and some answers are not one of the five. All inbound email switches to the router at 14:00. It is 13:05.
handover: The prompt says: 'Classify this ticket.' and then the ticket text.
The five queues are Outages, Billing, Meters, Moves and Other.
howItWorks: Pick a step from the action list: look, change, check or ship. Nothing you pick is typed or executed: every step shows an authored result.
Each step takes working minutes, and the clock moves by the minutes it takes. The deadline runs on the same clock.
Shipping is final for this case. Afterwards you record what you found and explain your reasoning.

parts.label: Why
parts.criteria: Temperature controls how likely the model is to choose lower-probability options; at 1.0 a classifier varies, and an open prompt lets it invent labels.

parts.criteria: Listed the five labels with examples, asked for the label only, set temperature 0 and a small maxTokens; lowering topP alone still varies; maxTokens caps length and does not affect consistency.

scoring.modelReasoning: The same input producing different labels points at sampling. At temperature 1.0 the model often picks lower-probability options, and the prompt never states the allowed labels, so it also invents them. List the five labels with examples, ask for the label only, set temperature 0, and check the labeled test set and repeat runs. Lowering topP helps but still varies; raising maxTokens only allows longer answers.
